questions.stem: What type of context should metadata ideally provide for data?
options: A context limited to one department
A context that changes with every query
questions.explanation: The objective is to imbue data with context, and ideally that context is trustworthy and secure.

questions.stem: How many high-level steps are outlined for selecting mandatory metadata?
questions.explanation: Three high-level steps guide the selection: the 5W 1H method, three selection criteria and the six Golden Rules.

questions.stem: Which questions make up the 5W 1H method for choosing metadata?
options: Who, What, When, Where, Why and How
Who, Which, When, Where, Why and How much
What, Where, Why, Whether, While and How
Who, What, When, Where, Why and Hence
Where, When, Which, Why, Who and How many
questions.explanation: The 5W 1H method asks Who, What, When, Where, Why and How to choose metadata aligned with specific objectives.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the three selection criteria for filtering metadata?
questions.explanation: The three criteria are For Everyone, Anyone Can Create and Follow Standards.

questions.stem: What does the For Everyone criterion require of metadata?
options: That it be created only by the legal team
That it be visible to the public internet
That anyone can understand it, without being tied to a specific organisation or industry
That it be free of charge
That it be stored in every system
questions.explanation: For Everyone means choosing metadata anyone can understand, not tied to specific organisations or industries.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named as a recognised universal metadata standard?
questions.explanation: The recognised standards named are Dublin Core, MODS, PREMIS and MPEG-7.

questions.stem: How many Golden Rules act as the final gatekeepers for selected metadata?
questions.explanation: Six Golden Rules act as final gatekeepers, and chosen metadata should follow at least one of them.

questions.stem: Which Golden Rule says metadata should help users find data easily?
questions.explanation: Discoverability ensures users can quickly find and understand the data they need.

questions.stem: Which Golden Rule is about metadata following the rules and organisational guidelines for using data?
questions.explanation: Governance requires metadata to follow set rules so that it is consistent and aligned with organisational guidelines.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Reusability Golden Rule?
options: To make each piece of metadata stand out
To make others want to use the data again in different situations
To ensure metadata is accurate for decision-making
To explain why the data matters
To restrict metadata to a single use
questions.explanation: Reusability means designing metadata so it can be used in different situations, which makes data management more efficient.
